description: Seed taxonomy for Hamlet's Ghost taste memory. Entries are either seeded from Lumafox anti-pattern research or emergent from lab packet evidence. The compiler merges both sources; packet evidence always takes precedence over seed descriptions.
origin: Lumafox Anti-Pattern Taxonomy v1.0.0, adapted for comparative judgment

anti_patterns.description: Structural failure patterns in generated artifacts. Each entry describes a CLASS of failure — not a specific phrase but a recognizable structural formula. Patterns may apply to generation, evaluation, or both.

entries.name: The Antithetical Formula
entries.description: Any sentence where the first clause negates or sets up a reframe that the second clause delivers. The construction pre-digests the insight for the reader instead of letting juxtaposition do the work.
entries.why_it_fails: Hands the reader the turn rather than letting them discover it. Real prose lets the juxtaposition speak without scaffolding.
entries.correction_strategy: Place the two ideas next to each other and trust the reader.
examples_bad: He doesn't just avoid the game — he builds an entire theology around refusal.
This isn't about politics — it's about the stories we tell ourselves.
examples_good: He builds an entire theology around refusal.

entries.name: Formulaic Parallel Construction
entries.template: turns his X into Y, his A into B
entries.description: Stacked parallel phrases where each element maps one domain onto another in the same grammatical frame. Looks like craft but is assembly-line rhetoric.
entries.why_it_fails: The parallel structure does the thinking for the reader. Each pair clicks into place too neatly. One strong observation is enough if it's the right one.
entries.correction_strategy: Commit to one strong observation. Let it breathe.
examples_bad: turns his paralysis into a moral system, his fear into a philosophy
where others see failure he finds vindication, where they see weakness he builds strength
examples_good: His paralysis becomes a moral system.

entries.name: Stacked Poetic Devices
entries.template: metaphor + alliteration + parallel in one sentence
entries.description: Multiple rhetorical devices layered into a single sentence, producing something that reads like prize prose but says nothing precise.
entries.why_it_fails: Poetic density without earned context. Each device competes for attention. The sentence becomes about its own cleverness rather than its subject.
entries.correction_strategy: One device per sentence, chosen because it reveals something.
examples_bad: wear their weakness like a scar they refuse to powder over
the silence between them grew teeth and learned to bite

entries.name: The Reframe Pivot
entries.template: The real [noun] isn't X — it's Y
entries.description: Claims to reveal what something is really about by negating the obvious reading and substituting a deeper one. A formula for appearing insightful.
entries.why_it_fails: The 'real X' construction promises depth but delivers a pivot the reader can see coming by the third word.
entries.correction_strategy: State the deeper reading directly. If it's true, it doesn't need theatrical setup.
examples_bad: The real tragedy isn't his death — it's that he saw it coming.
What matters here isn't the betrayal — it's the silence that followed.

entries.name: Hedged Profundity
entries.description: Signals depth without committing to a specific observation. The adjective slot can be filled with almost anything, which is the tell — if the frame works with any adjective, the frame is doing the work, not the thought.
entries.why_it_fails: The construction gestures at meaning without producing it. It's a placeholder for insight.
entries.correction_strategy: Name the specific thing. Replace the hedge with the observation itself.
examples_bad: There's something almost sacred about the way he refuses to answer.
There's something deeply unsettling about this silence.
examples_good: His refusal to answer has become a kind of liturgy.

entries.name: Over-Expansion
entries.description: Three paragraphs when one would do. The output restates, elaborates, and re-summarizes the same point without adding information.
entries.why_it_fails: Dilutes the strongest version of the idea. The best sentence gets buried in its own echoes.
entries.correction_strategy: Say it once, say it well, stop.

entries.name: Performative Confidence
entries.description: Business-lane outputs that project certainty without evidence. Assertions about market position, user needs, or strategic direction that sound authoritative but rest on nothing specific.
entries.why_it_fails: Trustworthy business writing earns confidence through specificity. Performed confidence reads as empty to anyone who knows the domain.
entries.correction_strategy: Replace assertions with evidence. If the evidence doesn't exist, say so.
examples_bad: Our unique approach positions us perfectly to capture this market.
Users are increasingly demanding exactly this kind of solution.
examples_good: Three of our five pilot customers renewed without a sales call.

entries.name: Generic Reassurance
entries.description: Business-lane outputs that soothe rather than inform. Retention emails, apology copy, and strategy memos that could apply to any company because they say nothing specific to this one.
entries.why_it_fails: Reassurance without specificity reads as form letter. The reader recognizes the template.
entries.correction_strategy: Name the specific situation, the specific loss, the specific remedy. If it could be sent by any company, rewrite it.
examples_bad: We value your feedback and are committed to continuous improvement.
We understand your frustration and want you to know we're working on it.
examples_good: The export bug that hit your Thursday report is fixed. Here's what happened.

quality_signals.description: Positive patterns that indicate genuine craft. These are what the lab rewards, not just what it penalizes. Quality signals are harder to codify than anti-patterns because they depend on context, but recurring human preferences point to these.

entries.name: Earned Metaphor
entries.description: A single extended metaphor that the artifact commits to and develops, rather than stacking multiple metaphors for density. The metaphor earns its place by revealing something about the subject.
entries.why_it_works: Commitment to one metaphor creates coherence. The reader follows one thread of meaning rather than being dazzled by many.

entries.name: Showing Not Telling
entries.description: The artifact conveys its subject through scene, atmosphere, and implication rather than explicit statement. The concept inhabits the text even if the label word never appears.
entries.why_it_works: Treats the reader as intelligent. Creates texture and experience rather than summary. The LVF-50 baseline found that naive evaluation penalizes this — which means evaluators must be calibrated to recognize it.
entries.evaluator_note: Evaluators that check for keyword presence will systematically penalize the best instances of this signal. See LVF-50 Finding 1.

entries.name: Specific Detail Over Generic Claim
entries.description: The artifact uses concrete, particular details rather than abstract assertions. Names, numbers, textures, specific situations rather than categorical statements.
entries.why_it_works: Specificity is the fastest signal of real knowledge. Generic claims can be produced by any model; specific details require either real knowledge or genuine imaginative commitment.

entries.name: Trustworthy Tone
entries.description: Business writing that earns trust through candor, specificity, and restraint rather than through polish and reassurance. Acknowledges limits. Names specifics. Does not oversell.
entries.why_it_works: Trust is built by saying less than you could, not more than you should. The reader trusts the writer who acknowledges what they don't know.

evaluator_failure_modes.description: Anti-patterns in evaluation rather than generation. These describe systematic ways automated judges misread artifact quality.

entries.name: Keyword Presence Bias
entries.description: Evaluators that check for explicit mention of assigned concepts rather than atmospheric or implied presence. Penalizes showing-not-telling. Rewards literal compliance over craft.
entries.why_it_fails: The best creative artifacts often convey their subject without naming it. An evaluator that demands the word 'ghost' will fail on the best ghost stories.
entries.correction_strategy: Evaluate semantic presence, not string presence. Does the concept inhabit the text even if the word doesn't?

entries.name: Coherence Over Life
entries.description: Evaluators that reward structural coherence and safety over vividness, risk, and emotional pressure. Produces a systematic preference for competent-but-flat over alive-but-uneven.
entries.why_it_fails: Coherence is necessary but not sufficient. An artifact can be perfectly coherent and completely forgettable. Human reviewers often prefer the artifact with more life, even if it's rougher.
entries.correction_strategy: When scoring, weight vividness and memorability alongside coherence. A safe artifact should not automatically outscore a vivid one.

entries.name: Novelty Penalty
entries.description: Evaluators that treat unfamiliar structures, unexpected tonal choices, or unconventional approaches as errors rather than as creative risk. Systematically conservative.
entries.why_it_fails: The most interesting artifacts are often the ones that don't fit the expected template. An evaluator calibrated on 'normal good' will miss 'surprisingly good.'
entries.correction_strategy: Distinguish between incoherent and unexpected. Penalize the former, investigate the latter.

entries.name: Rhetorical Situation Blindness
entries.description: Evaluators judge style and local craft without adequately considering audience, relation, stakes, or the obligations of the form. A move that works in a speech or manifesto gets overrated in a resignation letter, apology, or private note.
entries.why_it_fails: Good writing is situational. A judge that ignores rhetorical setting will reward force, repetition, or elevation where the form actually requires precision, candor, restraint, or intimacy.
entries.correction_strategy: Score rhetorical devices against audience and occasion. Ask what this piece owes its reader before rewarding intensity or flourish.

entries.name: Solemnity Halo
entries.description: Evaluators over-reward elevated seriousness, composed diction, and tasteful gravity as if these were evidence of real value or wisdom.
entries.why_it_fails: Serious tone can simulate significance. A judge under solemnity halo will confuse moral atmosphere with moral intelligence and mistake prestige aura for durable worth.
entries.correction_strategy: Ask what the artifact actually reveals, risks, or clarifies beyond tone. Treat seriousness as neutral until it is earned by pressure, insight, or exactness.

promotion_rules.description: Rules for when observations graduate to stable taxonomy entries.
promotion_rules.note: A pattern must appear across 3+ packets before it becomes a concept page. Promotion to a stable taxonomy entry additionally requires that the pattern is structurally identifiable as a class and has a documented correction strategy. Human confirmation is required for high-confidence status.
